(Continued)</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">respectively. The fair
value of the contracts outstanding at December&nbsp;31, 2006 and January&nbsp;1,
2006 was $35,000 and $71,000, respectively.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">At December&nbsp;31, 2006,
the Company held 70 contracts, four of them for December&nbsp;2006 and the
remainder spread over the first nine months of 2007. These contracts correspond
to approximately 20% of the Company&#146;s anticipated cream purchases for the
periods represented.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Advertising&#151;</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company expenses
advertising costs as incurred. For the years ended December&nbsp;31, 2006, January&nbsp;1,
2006 and January&nbsp;2, 2005, advertising expenses were $16,801,000,
$18,694,000 and $20,734,000, respectively.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Leases and Deferred
Straight-Line Rent Payable&#151;</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company leases many of its restaurant properties. Leases
are accounted for under the provisions of SFAS No.&nbsp;13, &#147;Accounting for
Leases,&#148; as amended, which requires that leases be evaluated and classified as
operating or capital leases for financial reporting purposes. The lease term
used for lease evaluation includes option periods only in instances in which
the exercise of the option period can be reasonably assured and failure to
exercise such options would result in an economic penalty. Leasehold
improvements that are acquired subsequent to the inception of a lease are
amortized over the lesser of the useful life of the asset or a term that
includes option periods that are reasonably assured at the date of the
purchase.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">For leases that contain rent escalations, the Company
records the total rent payable during the lease term, as determined above, on a
straight-line basis over the term of the lease and records the difference
between the rents paid and the straight-line rent as a deferred straight-line
rent payable.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Certain leases contain
provisions that require additional rental payments based upon restaurant sales
volume (&#147;contingent rentals&#148;). Contingent rentals are accrued each period as
the liabilities are incurred utilizing prorated periodic sales targets.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Lease Guarantees
and Contingencies&#151;</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Primarily as a result of
the Company&#146;s strategy to sell Company-operated restaurants to franchisees, the
Company remains liable for certain lease assignments and guarantees. These
leases have varying terms, the latest of which expires in 2020. As of December&nbsp;31,
2006, the potential amount of undiscounted payments the Company could be
required to make in the event of non-payment by the primary lessees was
$6,648,000. The present value of these potential payments discounted at the
Company&#146;s pre-tax cost of debt at December&nbsp;31, 2006 was $5,041,000. The
Company generally has cross-default provisions with franchisees that would put
them in default of their franchise agreement in the event of non-payment under
the lease. The Company believes these cross-default provisions significantly
reduce the risk that the Company will be required to make payments under these
leases and, historically, the Company had not been required to make such
payments. Accordingly, no liability has been recorded for exposure under such
leases at December&nbsp;31, 2006 and January&nbsp;1, 2006.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Net Income (Loss)
Per Share&#151;</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Basic net income (loss) per share is calculated by
dividing net income (loss) by the weighted average number of common shares
outstanding during the period. Diluted net income (loss) per share is
calculated by dividing net income (loss) by the weighted average number of
shares of common stock and common stock equivalents outstanding during the
period. Common stock equivalents are dilutive stock options and warrants that
are assumed exercised for calculation purposes. The number of common stock
options which could dilute basic earnings per share in the future, that were
not included in the computation of diluted income (loss) per share because to
do so would have been antidilutive, was 151,000, 273,000 and 320,000 for the
years ended December&nbsp;31, 2006, January&nbsp;1, 2006 and January&nbsp;2,
2005, respectively.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Presented
below is the reconciliation between basic and diluted weighted average shares

<p style="line-height:1.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Stock-Based
Compensation&#151;</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Prior to January&nbsp;2, 2006, the Company accounted
for stock-based compensation for employees under Accounting Principles
Board (&#147;APB&#148;) Opinion No.&nbsp;25, &#147;Accounting for Stock Issued to Employees,&#148;
and related interpretations. The Company had adopted the disclosure-only
provisions of SFAS No.&nbsp;123, &#147;Accounting for Stock-Based Compensation&#148;
and the disclosures required by SFAS No.&nbsp;148, &#147;Accounting for Stock-Based
Compensation&#151;Transition and Disclosure.&#148;&#160;
In accordance with APB Opinion No.&nbsp;25, the Company generally
recognized no stock-based compensation cost, as all options granted during that
period had an exercise price equal to the market value of the stock on the date
of grant. Stock-based compensation cost of $68,000 and $238,000 related to
modified option awards was included in net loss for the years ended January&nbsp;1,
2006 and January&nbsp;2, 2005, respectively, for the Company&#146;s 1997 Stock
Option Plan and the Company&#146;s 2003 Equity Incentive Plan.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On December&nbsp;16, 2004, the Financial Accounting
Standards Board (&#147;FASB&#148;) issued SFAS No.&nbsp;123 (revised 2004), &#147;Share-Based Payment&#148;<i>  </i>(&#147;SFAS No.&nbsp;123R&#148;). SFAS No.&nbsp;123R
supersedes APB Opinion No.&nbsp;25 and amends SFAS No.&nbsp;95, &#147;Statement of Cash Flows.&#148; Generally,
the approach in SFAS No.&nbsp;123R is similar to the approach described in SFAS
No.&nbsp;123. However, SFAS No.&nbsp;123R requires all share-based payments to
employees, including grants of employee stock options, to be recognized in the
income statement based on their fair values at the date of grant. Pro forma
disclosure is no longer an alternative.</font></p>


 <p style="margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">F-15</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">

<!-- SEQ.=1,FOLIO='F-15',FILE='C:\fc\64193847877_D11090_1813615\5770-1-fo.htm',USER='jmsproofassembler',CD='Mar  5 19:39 2007' -->
<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">
 <p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:16.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 24.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">FRIENDLY ICE CREAM CORPORATION AND SUBSIDIARIES<br> NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS (Continued)</font></b></p>


<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">2.
SUMMARY OF BASIS OF PRESENTATION AND SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES
(Continued)</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On January&nbsp;2, 2006
(the first day of its 2006 fiscal year), the Company adopted SFAS No.&nbsp;123R
using the modified prospective method as permitted under SFAS No.&nbsp;123R.
Under this transition method, compensation cost recognized for the year ended December&nbsp;31,
2006 included: (a)&nbsp;compensation cost for all share-based payments granted
prior to but not yet vested as of January&nbsp;1, 2006, based on the grant-date
fair value estimated in accordance with the provisions of SFAS No.&nbsp;123,
and (b)&nbsp;compensation cost for all share-based payments granted subsequent
to January&nbsp;1, 2006, based on the grant-date fair value estimated in
accordance with the provisions of SFAS No.&nbsp;123R. In accordance with the
modified prospective method of adoption, the Company&#146;s results of operations
and financial position for prior periods have not been restated.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Recently Issued
Accounting Pronouncements&#151;</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In July&nbsp;2006, the
FASB issued FASB Interpretation No.&nbsp;48, &#147;Accounting for Uncertainty in
Income Taxes&#151;an interpretation of FASB Statement No.&nbsp;109&#148; (&#147;FIN 48&#148;),
which clarifies the accounting for uncertainty in tax positions. FIN 48
requires that the Company recognize in its financial statements the impact of a
tax position, if that position is more likely than not of being sustained on
audit based on the technical merits of the position. The provisions of FIN 48
are effective as of the beginning of the Company&#146;s 2007 fiscal year, with the
cumulative effect of the change in accounting principle recorded as an
adjustment to opening retained earnings. The adoption of FIN 48 is not expected
to have a material effect on the Company&#146;s consolidated financial position or
results of operations.</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">3. STOCK BASED
COMPENSATION</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In 1997, the Board of Directors adopted a restricted
stock plan (the &#147;Restricted Stock Plan&#148;), pursuant to which 371,285 shares were
authorized for issuance. The Restricted Stock Plan provides for the award of
common stock, the vesting of which is subject to conditions and limitations
established by the Board of Directors. Such conditions may include continued
employment with the Company or the achievement of performance measures. Upon
the award of common stock, the participant has the rights of a stockholder,
including but not limited to the right to vote such stock and the right to
receive any dividends paid on such stock. The Board of Directors, in its sole
discretion, may designate employees and persons providing material services to
the Company as eligible for participation in the Restricted Stock Plan. In
connection with the approval of the 2003 Incentive Plan, discussed elsewhere
herein, the shares authorized for issuance under the Restricted Stock Plan were
reduced by 156,217 shares of stock.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The issued shares vested
on a straight-line basis over eight years or on an accelerated basis if certain
performance criteria were met. The Company recorded the fair value of the
shares issued at the issuance dates as compensation expense over the estimated
vesting periods. During the year ended January&nbsp;2, 2005, the Company
recorded stock compensation expense of $257,000, which was included in general
and administrative expenses in the accompanying consolidated statements of
operations.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Equity Compensation
Plans&#151;</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company currently grants stock awards under the

Stock Option Plan (&#147;1997 Plan&#148;)&#151;</font></i></font> The 1997 Plan was
adopted by the Company&#146;s Board of Directors and stockholders in November&nbsp;1997
and was subsequently amended on March&nbsp;27, 2000 and </p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><font style="font-size:10.0pt;">3. STOCK

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 20.0pt;text-indent:0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">October&nbsp;24, 2001.
Under the 1997 Plan, the Company&#146;s Board of Directors may grant options to
purchase up to 1,034,970 shares of common stock to employees, executive
officers and directors. The 1997 Plan provides for the issuance of nonqualified
stock options and incentive stock options (which are intended to satisfy the
requirements of Section&nbsp;422 of the Internal Revenue Code) and stock
appreciation rights (&#147;SARs&#148;). The Compensation Committee of the Board of
Directors determines the employees who will receive awards under the 1997 Plan
and the terms of such awards. The exercise price of a stock option or SAR
granted or awarded under the 1997 Plan may not be less than the fair market
value of one share of common stock on the date the stock option or SAR is
granted.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 20.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font style="font-style:italic;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The
2003 Equity Incentive Plan (the &#147;2003 Incentive Plan&#148;)&#151;</font></i></font>On
April&nbsp;9, 2003, the Board of Directors adopted an equity incentive plan,
which was approved by shareholders on May&nbsp;14, 2003. On May&nbsp;10, 2006,
the shareholders approved an amendment to the 2003 Incentive Plan to increase
the number of shares of common stock reserved for issuance under the 2003
Incentive Plan from 307,000 to 607,000 shares. The 2003 Incentive Plan provides for the issuance of
nonqualified stock options and incentive stock options (which are intended to
satisfy the requirements of Section&nbsp;422 of the Internal Revenue Code),
SARs, bonus stock, stock units, performance shares, performance units,
restricted stock and restricted stock units. The Compensation Committee of the
Board of Directors determines the employees who will receive awards under the
2003 Incentive Plan and the terms of such awards. The exercise price of a stock
option or SAR granted or awarded under the 2003 Incentive Plan may not be less
than the fair market value of one share of common stock on the date the stock
option or SAR is granted.</p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Outstanding options issued prior to December&nbsp;20,
2004 are fully vested. Options issued on and subsequent to December&nbsp;20,
2004 generally vest over three years. Options issued prior to July&nbsp;24,
2002 expire 10 years from the date of grant. Options issued subsequent to that
date have a five year expiration date.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As of December&nbsp;31,
2006, no SARs had been issued.</font></p>

 <p style="margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">F-17</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">
 <p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:16.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 24.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">FRIENDLY ICE CREAM CORPORATION AND SUBSIDIARIES<br> NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS (Continued)</font></b></p>


<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">3. STOCK
BASED COMPENSATION (Continued)</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Risk-free interest rate&#151;the yield on zero-coupon U.S.
Treasury securities for a period that is commensurate with the expected term
assumption is used as the risk-free interest rate.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Expected life&#151;the Company uses historical employee
exercise and option expiration data to estimate the expected life assumption
for the Black-Scholes grant-date valuation. The Company believes that this
historical data is currently the best estimate of the expected life of a new
option.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Expected volatility&#151;the Company is responsible for
estimating volatility and has used historical volatility to estimate the
grant-date fair value of stock options. Management considered the guidance in
SFAS No.&nbsp;123R and believes that the historical estimated volatility is
materially indicative of expectations about future volatility.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Expected dividend yield&#151;the
Company has not paid any dividends in the last five years and currently intends
to retain any earnings to finance future growth and, therefore, does not
anticipate paying any cash dividends on its common stock in the foreseeable
future.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Expense&#151;</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company used the straight-line attribution method
to recognize expense for all options granted. Stock-based compensation is
included in general and administrative expenses in the accompanying
consolidated statements of operations.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The amount of stock-based compensation recognized
during a period is based on the value of the portion of the awards that are
ultimately expected to vest. SFAS No.&nbsp;123R requires forfeitures to be
estimated at the time of grant and revised, if necessary, in subsequent periods
if actual forfeitures differ from those estimates. The term &#147;forfeitures&#148; is
distinct from &#147;cancellations&#148; or &#147;expirations&#148; and represents only the unvested
portion of the surrendered option. In September&nbsp;2006,
John Cutter, the Company&#146;s former President and Chief Executive Officer,
resigned. As of December&nbsp;31, 2006, the Company adjusted its stock
compensation expense to reflect his forfeitures. The Company will apply
an annual forfeiture rate to all options outstanding as of December&nbsp;31,
2006 and future options granted based on an analysis of its historical
forfeitures. This analysis will be re-evaluated quarterly and the forfeiture
rate will be adjusted as necessary. Ultimately, the actual expense recognized
over the vesting period will only be for those shares that vest.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The adoption of SFAS No.&nbsp;123R on January&nbsp;2,
2006 resulted in lower income from continuing operations, lower operating
income before tax and lower net income of $437,000 for the year ended December&nbsp;31,
2006. Additionally, the adoption of SFAS No.&nbsp;123R on January&nbsp;2, 2006
resulted in lower basic and diluted net income per share of $0.06 and $0.05,
respectively. </font>The total
income tax benefit recognized in the accompanying consolidated statement of
operations for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2006 for share-based
compensation arrangements was $2,000.</p>

<div style="margin:0pt 0pt .0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><hr size="1" width="160" noshade color="black" align="left" style="width:120.0pt;"></div>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt 20.0pt;text-indent:-20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(a)</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>On
December&nbsp;20, 2004, the Company&#146;s Board of Directors approved the vesting
of all outstanding and unvested options for the Company&#146;s Stock Option Plan and
the Company&#146;s 2003 Incentive Plan. This action was taken to reduce, or
eliminate to the extent permitted, the transition expense related to
outstanding stock option awards under SFAS No.&nbsp;123 (revised 2004), &#147;Share-Based
Payment&#148; (&#147;SFAS No.&nbsp;123R&#148;). The 259,850 options that were vested included
145,239 options with exercise prices greater than the Company&#146;s closing stock
price on the modification date. Under the accounting guidance of APB Opinion No.&nbsp;25,
the accelerated vesting resulted in stock-based compensation cost of $9,400
(net of related income tax benefit of $6,600), which was included in net loss
for the year ended January&nbsp;2, 2005. Additionally, the effect of the
accelerated vesting in the Company&#146;s pro-forma disclosure was incremental stock-based
compensation of approximately $666,000 (net of related income tax benefit of
$463,000). This stock-based compensation expense would otherwise have been
recognized in accordance with SFAS No.&nbsp;123R in the Company&#146;s consolidated
statements of operations over the next two fiscal years.</p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During the years ended December&nbsp;31, 2006, January&nbsp;1,
2006 and January&nbsp;2, 2005, the total intrinsic value of options exercised
(i.e., the difference between the market price at exercise and the price paid
by the employee to exercise the options) was $1,100,000, $1,097,000 and
$1,989,000, respectively and the total amount of cash received from exercise of
stock options was $1,143,000, $1,037,000 and $978,000, respectively.</font></p>

 <p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:16.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 24.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">FRIENDLY ICE CREAM CORPORATION AND SUBSIDIARIES<br> NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS (Continued)</font></b></p>


<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">3. STOCK
BASED COMPENSATION (Continued)</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As of December&nbsp;31, 2006, there was $547,000 of
unrecognized compensation cost related to unvested stock options. That cost is
expected to be recognized over a weighted-average period of 2.16 years.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The total fair value of shares vested during the years
ended December&nbsp;31, 2006, January&nbsp;1, 2006 and January&nbsp;2, 2005 was
$206,000, $0 and $1,519,000, respectively.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Pursuant to a stockholder
rights plan (the &#147;Stockholder Rights Plan&#148;) that FICC adopted in 1997, the
Board of Directors declared a dividend distribution of one purchase right (a &#147;Right&#148;)
for each outstanding share of common stock. The Stockholder Rights Plan
provides, in substance, that should any person or group (other than certain
management and affiliates) acquire 15% or more of FICC&#146;s common stock, each
Right, other than Rights held by the acquiring person or group, would entitle
its holder to purchase a specified number of shares of common stock for 50% of
their then current market value. Until a 15% acquisition has occurred, the
Rights may be redeemed by FICC at any time prior to the termination of the
Stockholder Rights Plan.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Restricted Stock
Unit Activity&#151;</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On December&nbsp;2, 2005, 30,000 restricted stock
units were issued to directors with a weighted average fair value of $8.90 at
grant date. On November&nbsp;1, 2006, 30,000 restricted stock units were issued
to directors with a weighted average fair value of $10.61 at grant date. The
restricted stock units were issued pursuant to and subject to the terms of the
Company&#146;s 2003 Incentive Plan. Subject to the terms of the 2003 Incentive Plan,
each restricted stock unit provides the holder with the right to receive one
share of Common Stock of the Company when the restrictions lapse or vest. The
restricted stock units granted to the directors vest three years after the date
of grant if the recipient is a member of the Company&#146;s Board of Directors on
such date, subject to accelerated vesting in the event of a change in control
or the director&#146;s death, disability or retirement.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During the years ended December&nbsp;31, 2006 and January&nbsp;1,
2006, stock-based compensation cost of $106,400 and $7,400, respectively, was
recorded related to these units. As of December&nbsp;31, 2006, there was
$471,500 of total unrecognized compensation cost related to unvested restricted
stock units. That cost is expected to be recognized over a weighted-average
period of 2.38 years.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Pursuant to a long-term incentive plan for fiscal 2006
approved by the Compensation Committee of the Board of Directors under the
Company&#146;s 2003 Incentive Plan, the Compensation Committee established target
EBITDA levels for the Company for fiscal 2006 and target awards for each
officer named below based on a percentage (ranging from 50% to 100%) of each
such officer&#146;s base salary.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2006,
stock-based compensation of $98,000 was recorded related to the foregoing
awards.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On February&nbsp;28, 2007 the Compensation Committee
determined that the Company exceeded the threshold EBITDA for fiscal 2006, and
awarded shares of Common Stock under the Company&#146;s 2003 Incentive Plan to each
of the officers named below. The number of shares of Common Stock issued to
each officer was determined by dividing the officer&#146;s 2006 Award Value by 90%
of the closing price of the Company&#146;s Common Stock on the date of grant as
reported on the American Stock Exchange. 25% of the shares of Common Stock
issued to each officer are fully vested upon issuance. The remaining 75% of the
shares of Common Stock will vest in three equal annual installments following
issuance if the officer remains employed by the Company. The unvested shares
will also fully vest upon a change in control, as provided in the 2003
Incentive Plan.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The
following table sets forth each officer&#146;s 2006 Award Value and the number of
shares of Common Stock the officer received under the long-term incentive plan
for fiscal 2006.</font></p>

<p style="line-height:1.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Upon the sale of the Company by Hershey Foods
Corporation (&#147;Hershey&#148;) in 1988, all of the trademarks and service marks used
in the Company&#146;s business at that time which did not contain the word &#147;Friendly&#148;
(the &#147;Non-Friendly Marks&#148;) were licensed by Hershey to the Company. The
Non-Friendly Marks license agreement fee was being amortized over the term of
the agreement, which expired on September&nbsp;2, 2028. In September&nbsp;2002,
Hershey assigned the Non-Friendly Marks to the Company. The Company will
continue to amortize the Non-Friendly Marks license agreement fee over the
original term of 40 years. The Company reviews the estimated future cash flows
related to each trademarked product on a quarterly basis to determine whether
any impairment has occurred. For the years ended December&nbsp;31, 2006, January&nbsp;1,
2006 and January&nbsp;2, 2005, no impairments were recorded.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In February&nbsp;2004, the Company announced a cash
tender offer and consent solicitation for $175,977,000 of its then outstanding
10.5% senior notes. In connection with the tender offer, the Company wrote off
unamortized deferred financing costs for the purchase of the 10.5% senior notes
in March&nbsp;2004 and the redemption of the remaining 10.5% senior notes in April&nbsp;2004
of $1,788,000 and $657,000, respectively. The $2,445,000 was included in other
(income) expense in the accompanying consolidated statement of operations for
the year ended January&nbsp;2, 2005. Additionally, the Company incurred
$6,374,000 of costs associated with the issuance of new 8.375% senior notes and
the amendment to the </font></p>


 <p style="margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">F-23</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">
 <p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:16.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 24.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">FRIENDLY ICE CREAM CORPORATION AND SUBSIDIARIES<br> NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS (Continued)</font></b></p>


<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><font style="font-size:10.0pt;">4.
INTANGIBLE ASSETS AND DEFERRED COSTS</font> (Continued)</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">revolving credit facility,
which were included in intangible assets and deferred costs in the accompanying
consolidated balance sheets as of December&nbsp;31, 2006 and January&nbsp;1,
2006. These costs are being amortized over the terms of the 8.375% senior notes
and the Credit Facility.</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">5. ASSET IMPAIRMENT AND
DISCONTINUED OPERATIONS</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During 2005, the Company disposed of five properties
by sale and nine properties other than by sale, including lease terminations. During
December&nbsp;2005, the Company closed seven restaurants and committed to a
plan to sell those seven restaurants as well as four restaurants that were
closed in 2004. At January&nbsp;1, 2006, these 11 properties met the criteria
for &#147;held for sale&#148; as defined in SFAS No.&nbsp;144, &#147;Accounting for the
Impairment or Disposal of Long-Lived Assets.&#148; During 2006, the Company sold
eight of these 11 properties. Net proceeds from these transactions were
$6,855,000. The Company recognized a net gain related to the sales of the
assets of $4,359,000. At December&nbsp;31, 2006, the remaining three properties
and one property that closed in 2006 met the criteria for &#147;held for sale&#148; as
defined in SFAS No.&nbsp;144. The carrying values of these four properties of
$896,000, and $933,000 as of December&nbsp;31, 2006 and January&nbsp;1, 2006,
respectively, were reported as assets held for sale in the accompanying
consolidated balance sheets. The carrying values of these properties were not
adjusted since the carrying values were less than the estimated fair market
values less costs to sell.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">SFAS No.&nbsp;144 requires the results of operations
of a component of an entity that is classified as held for sale or that has
been disposed of to be reported as discontinued operations in the statement of
operations if certain conditions are met. These conditions include commitment
to a plan of disposal after the effective date of this statement, elimination
of the operations and cash flows of the entity component from the ongoing
operations of the Company and no significant continuing involvement in the
operations of the entity component after the disposal transaction.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In
accordance with SFAS No.&nbsp;144, the results of operations of the eight
properties that were disposed of during 2006 and the 14 properties that were
disposed of during 2005, and any related net gain on the disposals, as well as
the results of operations of three properties held for sale at December&nbsp;31,
2006 were reported separately as discontinued operations in the accompanying
consolidated statements of operations for all years presented. For the years
ended December&nbsp;31, 2006, January&nbsp;1, 2006 and January&nbsp;2, 2005,
these discontinued results consisted of the following (in thousands):</font></p>

 <p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:16.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 24.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">FRIENDLY ICE CREAM CORPORATION AND SUBSIDIARIES<br> NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS (Continued)</font></b></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">5. ASSET IMPAIRMENT AND
DISCONTINUED OPERATIONS (Continued)</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During 2006, the Company disposed of two properties by
sale and two properties other than by sale, including lease terminations.
Additionally, the Company closed one restaurant and committed to a plan to sell
that restaurant. At December&nbsp;31, 2006, this property met the criteria for
&#147;held for sale&#148; as defined in SFAS No.&nbsp;144. The results of operations and
any related gain or loss associated with the disposition of these restaurants
were not material and therefore were reported within continuing operations in
the accompanying consolidated statements of operations for all years presented.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During 2004, the
Company disposed of two properties by sale and one property other than by sale.
The results of operations and any related gain or loss associated with
the disposition of these restaurants were not material and therefore were
reported within continuing operations in 2004.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During 2006, the Company determined that the carrying
values of three operating restaurant properties exceeded their estimated fair
values less costs to sell and the carrying values were reduced by an aggregate
of $719,000 accordingly.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During the year ended January&nbsp;1, 2006, the
Company determined that the carrying values of six restaurant properties and
certain capital inventory used to replace restaurant equipment exceeded their
estimated fair values less costs to sell. The carrying values were reduced by
an aggregate of $2,478,000.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During the year ended January&nbsp;2,
2005, the Company determined that the carrying value of a vacant restaurant
land parcel and the carrying value of one restaurant property exceeded their
estimated fair values less costs to sell. The carrying values were reduced by
an aggregate of $91,000.</font></p>

<p style="line-height:1.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In December&nbsp;2001, the Company completed a
financial restructuring plan which included the repayment of all amounts
outstanding under its then existing credit facility and the purchase of
approximately $21,273,000 of its 10.5% senior notes with the proceeds from
$55,000,000 in long-term mortgage financing (the &#147;Mortgage Financing&#148;) and a
$33,700,000 sale and leaseback transaction (the &#147;Sale/Leaseback Financing&#148;).</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Interest on $10,000,000 of the original $55,000,000
from the Mortgage Financing is variable (&#147;Variable Mortgages&#148;) and the
remaining $45,000,000 of the original $55,000,000 from the Mortgage Financing
bears interest at a fixed annual rate of 10.16% (&#147;Fixed Mortgages&#148;). The Fixed
Mortgages have a maturity date of January&nbsp;1, 2022 and are amortized over
20 years.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On December&nbsp;30, 2005, the Company completed a
refinancing of the Variable Mortgages (the &#147;Variable Refinancing&#148;). Under the
terms of the loan agreement for the Variable Refinancing, the Company borrowed
an aggregate sum of $8,500,000 at a variable interest rate equal to the sum of
the 90-day LIBOR rate in effect (5.36% at December&nbsp;31, 2006) plus 4%
on an annual basis. Changes in the interest rate are calculated monthly and
recognized annually when the monthly payment amount is adjusted. Changes in the
monthly payment amounts owed due to interest rate changes are reflected in the
principal balances, which are re-amortized over the remaining life of the
mortgages. The loans under the Variable Mortgages have a maturity date of January&nbsp;1,
2020 and are being amortized over 14 years.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In connection with the Variable Refinancing, the
Company incurred direct expenses of $71,300 that were included in the
accompanying consolidated statement of operations for the year ended January&nbsp;1,
2006 and $186,600 of costs that were included in intangible assets and deferred
costs in the accompanying </font></p>


 <p style="margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">F-26</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">
 <p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:16.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 24.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">FRIENDLY ICE CREAM CORPORATION AND SUBSIDIARIES<br> NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS (Continued)</font></b></p>


<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><font style="font-size:10.0pt;">6. DEBT</font>
(Continued)</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">consolidated balance
sheets as of December&nbsp;31, 2006 and January&nbsp;1, 2006. These costs are
being amortized over the term of the Variable Mortgages.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Pursuant to the terms of the Mortgage Financing, the
Company may sell properties securing its obligations provided that other
properties are substituted in place of the sold properties. The substituted
properties must meet certain requirements under the terms of the Mortgage
Financing. In August&nbsp;2005, proceeds of $415,000 and $2,650,000 were
received in connection with the sale of two mortgaged properties, of which
$400,000 and $1,250,000 of such amounts was placed in escrow pending the
inclusion of a substitute property. As of January&nbsp;1, 2006, these balances
were held as collateral and were included in restricted cash on the
accompanying consolidated balance sheet as of January&nbsp;1, 2006. In
connection with the Variable Refinancing, the mortgage on one of these
properties was released and the remaining $400,000 related to the sale of this property
was released from escrow during the first quarter of 2006. A substitute
property for the second property was obtained during the second quarter of 2006
in compliance with the substitution agreement. On June&nbsp;15, 2006, the
remaining $1,250,000 was released from escrow.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">All mortgage financings are subject to annual
covenants, including various minimum fixed charge coverage ratios. The Company
was in compliance with the covenants for the Variable Mortgages and Fixed
Mortgages as of December&nbsp;31, 2006.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In 2003 and 2004, the Company purchased or redeemed
all of its remaining outstanding 10.5% senior notes in a series of
transactions. In February&nbsp;2004, the Company announced a cash tender offer
and consent solicitation for $176,000,000 of its 10.5% senior notes which was
financed with the proceeds from a $175,000,000 private offering of new 8.375%
senior notes (the &#147;Senior Notes&#148;), available cash and its Credit Facility. In March&nbsp;2004,
$127,357,000 of aggregate principal amount of the 10.5% senior notes was
purchased at the tender offer and consent solicitation price of 104% of the
principal amount and $476,000 of aggregate principal amount of 10.5% senior
notes were purchased at the tender offer price of 102% of the principal amount.
In April&nbsp;2004, the remaining $48,144,000 of the 10.5% senior notes was
redeemed in accordance with the 10.5% senior notes indenture at 103.5% of the
principal amount.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The $175,000,000 of Senior Notes issued in March&nbsp;2004
are unsecured senior obligations of FICC, guaranteed on an unsecured senior
basis by FICC&#146;s Friendly&#146;s Restaurants Franchise,&nbsp;Inc. subsidiary, but are
effectively subordinated to all secured indebtedness of FICC, including the
indebtedness incurred under the Company&#146;s Credit Facility. The Senior Notes
mature on June&nbsp;15, 2012. Interest on the Senior Notes is payable at 8.375%
per annum semi-annually on June&nbsp;15 and December&nbsp;15 of each year.
The Senior Notes are redeemable, in whole or in part, at any time on or after June&nbsp;15,
2008 at FICC&#146;s option at redemption prices from 104.188% to 100.00%, based on
the redemption date. In addition, at any time prior to June&nbsp;15, 2007, FICC
may redeem, subject to certain conditions, up to 35% of the aggregate principal
amount of the Senior Notes with the proceeds of one or more qualified equity
offerings, as defined, at a redemption price of 108.375% of the principal
amount, plus accrued interest.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company has a $35,000,000 Credit Facility which is
available for borrowings to provide working capital, for issuances of letters
of credit and for other corporate needs. As of December&nbsp;31, 2006 and January&nbsp;1,
2006, total letters of credit outstanding were $15,474,000 and $15,974,000,
respectively. During 2006 and 2005, there were no drawings against the letters
of credit. The revolving credit loans bear interest at the Company&#146;s option at
either (a)&nbsp;the base rate plus the applicable margin as in effect from time
to time (the &#147;Base Rate&#148;) (10.25% at December&nbsp;31, 2006) or (b)&nbsp;the
Eurodollar rate plus the applicable margin as in effect from time to time (the &#147;Eurodollar
Rate&#148;) (9.32% at December&nbsp;31, 2006). As of </font></p>

 <p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:16.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 24.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">FRIENDLY ICE CREAM CORPORATION AND SUBSIDIARIES<br> NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS (Continued)</font></b></p>


<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">6. DEBT
(Continued)</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">December&nbsp;31, 2006 and
January&nbsp;1, 2006, there were no revolving credit loans outstanding. As of December&nbsp;31,
2006 and January&nbsp;1, 2006, $19,526,000 and $19,026,000, respectively, was
available for borrowing.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Credit Facility has an annual &#147;clean-up&#148; provision
which obligates the Company to repay in full any and all outstanding revolving
credit loans for a period of not less than 15 consecutive days during the
period beginning on or after May&nbsp;1 and ending on or before June&nbsp;15
(or the next business day, if, in any year, June&nbsp;15 is not a business day)
of each calendar year, such that immediately following the date of such repayment,
the amount of all outstanding revolving credit loans shall be zero.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Credit Facility includes certain restrictive
covenants including limitations on indebtedness, restricted payments such as
dividends and stock repurchases, liens, mergers, investments and sales of
assets and of subsidiary stock. Additionally, the Credit Facility limits the
amount which the Company may spend on capital expenditures, restricts the use
of proceeds, as defined, from asset sales and requires that the Company comply
with certain financial covenants. The Company</font> was in compliance with the covenants in
the Credit Facility as of December&nbsp;31, 2006.</p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On August&nbsp;1, 2006, the Company amended its
$35,000,000 Credit Facility to, among other things, (i)&nbsp;extend the
maturity date from June&nbsp;30, 2007 to June&nbsp;30, 2010, (ii)&nbsp;eliminate
the interest coverage requirement and (iii)&nbsp;reduce by 0.50% to 0.75% the
applicable margin rates at which the revolving credit loans bear interest to a
range of 3.00% to 4.00% (depending on the leverage ratio).</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><font style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company incurred
$519,000 </font>of costs associated with this amendment to the $35,000,000
Credit Facility which were deferred and are being amortized over the life of
the amended $35,000,000 Credit Facility.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The financial covenant

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 20.0pt;text-indent:-20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(a)</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>The Credit Facility&#146;s
definition of capital expenditures differs from the Company&#146;s total capital
expenditures.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 20.0pt;text-indent:-20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(b)</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>The Credit Facility&#146;s
definition of consolidated EBITDA allows non-cash losses and capitalized
interest to be added back to net income (loss) which differs from the Company&#146;s
adjusted EBITDA computation presented elsewhere herein.</p>

<p style="line-height:1.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The fair values of the
Senior Notes were determined based on the actual trade prices occurring closest
to December&nbsp;31, 2006 and January&nbsp;1, 2006. Because the mortgage loans
are privately held, the Company believes that the carrying value of the
mortgage loans as of December&nbsp;31, 2006 and January&nbsp;1, 2006
approximated the fair value.</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">7. LEASES</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As of December&nbsp;31,
2006 and January&nbsp;1, 2006, the Company operated 316 and 314 restaurants,
respectively. These operations were conducted in premises owned or leased as
follows:</font></p>

<p style="line-height:1.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Restaurants in shopping centers are generally leased
for a term of 10 to 20 years. Leases of freestanding restaurants generally are
for a 15 or 20 year lease term and provide for renewal options for three or four
five-year renewals at the then current fair market value. Additionally,
the Company leases certain equipment over lease terms from three to seven
years.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In connection with the Sale/Leaseback Financing in December&nbsp;2001,
the Company sold 44 properties operating as Friendly&#146;s restaurants and entered
into a master lease with the buyer to lease the 44 properties for an initial
term of 20 years under a triple net lease. There are four five-year renewal
options and lease payments are subject to escalator provisions every five years
based upon increases in the Consumer Price Index. In accordance with SFAS No.&nbsp;66,
&#147;Accounting for Sales of Real Estate&#148; and SFAS No.&nbsp;98, &#147;Accounting for
Leases&#148;, the Company recognized an aggregate loss of $428,000 on two properties
which was included in loss on disposals of other properties and equipment, net
in 2001. The aggregate gain of $11,377,000 on the remaining 42 properties was
deferred and the unamortized balance of $10,050,000 was included in other
accrued expenses and other long-term liabilities. The deferred gain is being
amortized straight-line over 20 years.</font></p>

and tax bases of the assets and liabilities multiplied by the enacted tax rates
in effect for the year in which the differences are expected to reverse.

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As of December&nbsp;31, 2006, the Company had
approximately $28,357,000 of net deferred tax assets relating to net operating
loss carryforwards, tax credit carryforwards and other temporary differences
that </font></p>


 <p style="margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">F-32</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">

<!-- SEQ.=1,FOLIO='F-32',FILE='C:\fc\6410516723_D11090_1810911\5770-1-fu.htm',USER='jmsproofassembler',CD='Mar  5 10:06 2007' -->
<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">
 <p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:16.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 24.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">FRIENDLY ICE CREAM CORPORATION AND SUBSIDIARIES<br> NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS (Continued)</font></b></p>


<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">8. INCOME
TAXES (Continued)</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">are available to reduce
income taxes in future years. SFAS No.&nbsp;109 &#147;Accounting for Income Taxes&#148;
requires that a valuation allowance be established when it is &#147;more likely than
not&#148; that all or a portion of deferred tax assets will not be realized. A
review of all available positive and negative evidence needs to be considered,
including a company&#146;s performance, the market environment in which the company
operates, length of carryback and carryforward periods, and projections of
future operating results. Where there are cumulative losses in recent years,
SFAS No.&nbsp;109 creates a strong presumption that a valuation allowance is
needed. The presumption can be overcome in very limited circumstances.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As of January&nbsp;1, 2006, the Company had
approximately $32,144,000 of net deferred tax assets relating to net operating
loss carryforwards, tax credit carryforwards and other temporary differences
that were available to reduce income taxes in future years.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During the fourth quarter of 2005, the Company entered
a three-year cumulative loss position and revised its projections of the amount
and timing of profitability in future periods. As a result, the Company
increased its valuation allowance by approximately $26,729,000 ($22,184,000 to
income tax expense and $4,545,000 to stockholders&#146; deficit) to reduce the
carrying value of net deferred tax assets to zero.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As of December&nbsp;31, 2006 the Company remains in a
three-year cumulative loss position and expects to record valuation allowances
on future tax benefits until it can sustain an appropriate level of
profitability. However, the Company has incurred approximately $1,093,000 of
federal tax liabilities for 2005 and 2006 combined. Approximately $928,000 of
the $1,093,000 would be available for refund if 2007 resulted in a loss for
income tax purposes. As a result, the valuation allowances as of December&nbsp;31,
2006 of $27,429,000 will reduce the carrying value of net deferred tax assets
to $928,000. Should the Company&#146;s future profitability provide sufficient
evidence, in accordance with SFAS No.&nbsp;109, to support the ultimate
realization of income tax benefits attributable to NOL and credit carryforwards
and other deductible temporary differences, a reduction in the valuation
allowance may be recorded and the carrying value of deferred tax assets may be
restored, resulting in a non-cash credit to earnings.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The income tax provision for the year ended December&nbsp;31,
2006 included a decrease in the valuation allowance of $797,000.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The income tax provision for the year ended January&nbsp;1,
2006 included the above referenced increase in the valuation allowance of
$22,184,000 and an increase in income tax accruals of $1,446,000 related to
ongoing tax audits and other tax matters. The increase in the valuation
allowance and the increase in income tax accruals accounted for 292.1% and
19.0%, respectively, of the Company&#146;s effective tax rate of 263.5%.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2006, the
Company generated federal taxable income of approximately $12,025,000. During
the year ended January&nbsp;1, 2006, the Company generated federal taxable
income of approximately $926,000. The Company had aggregate state NOL
carryforwards, the tax effect of which was approximately $1,684,000 and
$3,732,000 as of December&nbsp;31, 2006 and January&nbsp;1, 2006, respectively.
The state NOL carryforwards expire between 2007 and 2025. The tax effect of
state NOL carryforwrds expired by the end of 2006 without being used was
approximately $1,745,000. That portion of the valuation allowance specifically
allocated to these state NOLs was reduced accordingly.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As of December&nbsp;31, 2006 and January&nbsp;1, 2006,
the Company had federal general business credit carryforwards of $7,757,000 and
$9,535,000, respectively, which expire between 2020 and 2026. The </font></p>


 <p style="margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">F-33</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">

<!-- SEQ.=1,FOLIO='F-33',FILE='C:\fc\6410516723_D11090_1810911\5770-1-fu.htm',USER='jmsproofassembler',CD='Mar  5 10:06 2007' -->
<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">
 <p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:16.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 24.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">FRIENDLY ICE CREAM CORPORATION AND SUBSIDIARIES<br> NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS (Continued)</font></b></p>


<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">8. INCOME
TAXES (Continued)</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Company had $3,051,000 and
$2,721,000 of state tax credit carryforwards as of December&nbsp;31, 2006 and January&nbsp;1,
2006, respectively, which either expire between 2007 and 2011 or have no
expiration date.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Taxes payable were reduced
or refundable taxes, credit carryforwards and state loss carryforwards were
increased by an aggregate of $145,000 and $450,000 in 2006 and 2005,
respectively, as a result of stock options exercised.</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">9<font style="letter-spacing:-.1pt;">. </font>RESTRUCTURINGS</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During March&nbsp;2004, the Company recorded a pre-tax
restructuring charge of $2,627,000 for severance and outplacement services
associated with reduction in force actions taken during the first quarter of 2004
that reduced headcount by approximately 20 permanent positions.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On October&nbsp;10, 2001, the Company eliminated
approximately 70 positions at corporate headquarters. In addition,
approximately 30 positions in the restaurant construction and fabrication areas
were eliminated by December&nbsp;30, 2001. The purpose of the reduction was to
streamline functions and reduce redundancy among its business segments.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In March&nbsp;2000, the Company&#146;s Board of Directors
approved a restructuring plan that provided for the immediate closing of 81
restaurants at the end of March&nbsp;2000 and the disposition of an additional
70 restaurants over the next 24 months.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company reduced the restructuring reserves by
$400,000 and $1,900,000 during the years ended December&nbsp;29, 2002 and December&nbsp;30,
2001, respectively, since the reserve exceeded estimated remaining payments.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The
following represents the reserve and activity associated with the March&nbsp;2004,
October&nbsp;2001 and March&nbsp;2000 restructurings (in thousands):</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 5.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During 2006, three

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 5.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During 2005, the Company

existing Company-operated restaurants and agreed to develop a total of 10 new

$4,102,000, of which $295,000 was for franchise and development fees and
$3,807,000 was for the sale of certain assets and leasehold rights. During the
year ended January&nbsp;1, 2006, the Company recorded $210,000 of franchise fee
revenue for the initial locations acquired by franchisees and deferred $85,000

restaurants<font style="letter-spacing:-.1pt;"> are opened. In addition, the
Company recognized a gain of $2,712,000 related to the sale of assets.</font></font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 5.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During 2004, two
franchisees operating restaurants under options to purchase elected to exercise
their options. In doing so, they purchased six existing restaurants and
committed to develop a total of five new restaurants over the next six years
with an option to open an additional five restaurants in the following five
years. Gross proceeds from these transactions were $1,360,000, of which
$275,000 was for franchise and development fees and $1,085,000 was for the sale
of certain assets and leasehold rights. During the year ended January&nbsp;2,
2005, the Company recorded $200,000 of franchise fee revenue for the initial
locations acquired by these franchisees and deferred $75,000 related to future
development. The $75,000 will be recognized into income as restaurants<font style="letter-spacing:-.1pt;"> are opened. In addition, the Company recognized a
gain of $542,000 related to the sale of assets.</font></font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 5.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On September&nbsp;9, 2004,
the Company entered into an agreement granting NL Ark Development,&nbsp;Inc. (&#147;NL
Ark&#148;) certain limited exclusive rights to operate and develop Friendly&#146;s
Restaurants in designated areas within Palm Beach County, Florida. NL Ark has
committed to open five new Friendly&#146;s Restaurants over the next five years. The
Company received development fees of $80,000, which represent one-half of
future franchise fees. The $80,000 will be recognized into income as
restaurants are opened.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 8.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On January&nbsp;15, 2004,
the Company entered into an agreement granting Central Florida Restaurants LLC
(&#147;Central Florida&#148;) certain limited exclusive rights to operate and develop
Friendly&#146;s full-service restaurants in designated areas within the Orlando,
Florida market (the &#147;Central Florida Agreement&#148;). Pursuant to the Central
Florida Agreement, Central Florida purchased certain equipment assets, lease
and sublease rights and franchise rights in 10 existing Friendly&#146;s restaurants
and committed to open an additional 10 restaurants over the six years following
the date of the agreement with an option for 15 more restaurants in the
following five years. Gross proceeds from the sale were approximately
$3,150,000 of </font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">10.

$310,000 was for franchise fees for the initial 10 restaurants. In 2004, the
Company recorded $310,000 as franchise fee revenue and recognized a gain of
approximately $679,000 related to the sale of the assets for the 10 locations.
During the year ended January&nbsp;1, 2006, Central Florida opened two new
restaurants. In December&nbsp;2006, Central Florida defaulted under its leases
and franchise agreements and peaceably surrendered 11 restaurants to the
Company and closed one restaurant. The Company is currently operating the 11
restaurants for a limited period of time while the parties seek a substitute
franchisee to take over the operations at these restaurants.&nbsp;If the
properties are not franchised, the Company, at its option, may acquire or close
the restaurants.&nbsp;The Company and Central Florida&#146;s lenders and landlord
have entered into agreements pursuant to which the Company has agreed to make
recurring monthly rent and loan payments and the lenders and landlord have
agreed not to interfere with the Company operations&nbsp;while&nbsp;it&nbsp;operates
the restaurants. &#160;Except for the Company&#146;s
agreement to make certain payments while it is operating the restaurants, the
Company has not assumed any of Central Florida&#146;s obligations to its lender.</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 4.5pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">11.
PENSION PLAN</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 3.5pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Certain of the employees
of the Company are covered by a non-contributory defined benefit cash
balance pension plan. Plan benefits are based on years of service and
participant compensation during their years of employment.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 3.5pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Under the cash balance
plan, a nominal account for each participant was established. Through 2003, the
Company made an annual contribution to each participant&#146;s account based on
current wages and years of service. Each account earns a specified rate of
interest, which is adjusted annually. Plan expenses may also be paid from the
assets of the plan.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 3.5pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In 1997, pension benefits
were reduced to certain employees. In 1998, death benefits were increased. In
2002, pension benefits that were reduced in 1997 were restored to certain
employees. Also in 2002, pension benefits were reduced to all employees, to be
effective in 2003.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 3.5pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In November&nbsp;2003, the
Company announced that effective December&nbsp;31, 2003, all benefits accrued
under the pension plan would be frozen at the level attained on that date. The
benefits accrued through December&nbsp;31, 2003 were not reduced. As a result,
the Company recognized a one-time pension curtailment gain of $8,113,000 in
2003 equal to the unamortized balances as of December&nbsp;31, 2003 from all
plan changes made prior to that date. Cash balance accounts continue to be
credited with interest after December&nbsp;31, 2003.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 3.5pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During 2004, lump-sum cash
payments to participants exceeded the interest cost component of net periodic
pension cost. As a result of the unusual settlement volume, the Company
recorded additional pension expense of $2,204,000 during the year ended January&nbsp;2,
2005.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 4.5pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In October&nbsp;2006, the
FASB issued SFAS No.&nbsp;158, &#147;Employers&#146; Accounting for Defined Benefit
Pension and Other Postretirement Plans, an amendment of FASB Statements No.&nbsp;87,
88, 106 and 132(R)&#148; (&#147;SFAS No.&nbsp;158&#148;), which requires an entity to: (a)&nbsp;recognize
in its statement of financial position an asset for a defined benefit
postretirement plan&#146;s overfunded status or a liability for a plan&#146;s underfunded
status, (b)&nbsp;measure a defined benefit postretirement plan&#146;s assets and
obligations that determine its funded status as of the end of the employer&#146;s
fiscal year, and (c)&nbsp;recognize changes in the funded status of a defined
benefit postretirement plan in comprehensive income in the year in which the
changes occur. The requirement to recognize the funded status of a defined
benefit postretirement plan and the disclosure requirements are effective for
the Company&#146;s 2006 fiscal year.</font></p>

 <p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:16.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 24.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">FRIENDLY ICE CREAM CORPORATION AND SUBSIDIARIES<br> NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS (Continued)</font></b></p>


<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><font style="font-size:10.0pt;">11.
PENSION PLAN</font> (Continued)</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company determines its expected long-term rate of
return based on its expectations of future returns for the pension plan&#146;s
investments based on target allocations of the pension plan&#146;s investments.
Additionally, the Company considers historical returns on
comparable&nbsp;equity, fixed income and real estate investments and adjusts
its estimates as deemed appropriate. As of December&nbsp;31, 2006, point
estimates of the Company&#146;s long-term target allocation to equity (57.5%), fixed
income (32.0%), real estate (10.0%) and other (0.5%) is expected to provide
real rates of return of 7.23%, 2.21%, 1.90% and 1.50%, respectively. In
addition, the long-term inflation assumption was 3.75%. The resulting weighted
expected long-term rate of return on plan assets was 8.75%.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The
Company&#146;s pension plan weighted average asset allocations at December&nbsp;31,
2006 and January&nbsp;1, 2006 by asset category were as follows:</font></p>

<p style="line-height:1.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company actively manages its pension plan assets
utilizing a registered investment advisor as recognized under the Investment
Advisors Act of 1940, as amended. Oversight of the investment advisor is
provided by the Company&#146;s Qualified Benefit Plans Committee (&#147;QBPC&#148;). The plan&#146;s
trustee and investment advisor monitors transactions and performance monthly
and the QBPC reviews performance monthly with a complete review of plan assets
on a quarterly basis. Monthly, cash is withdrawn from the pension fund to meet
benefit requirements. This provides the investment advisor with an opportunity
to rebalance on a limited scale. If larger scale rebalancing is required, it is
performed on an as needed basis.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company believes that a moderately aggressive risk
posture is appropriate for the plan and is consistent with the
actuarially-determined cash payment requirements. Accordingly, the investment
of plan assets is governed by the Investment Policy of the Company&#146;s retirement
program which reflects two primary objectives: 1) achieving investment results
that will contribute to the proper funding of the plan, and 2) receiving from
its investment advisor performance that is above the average market return.
Asset mix guidelines exist within the Investment Policy that target equities at
30-80% of the portfolio, fixed income at 10-60% and real estate at
10%. It is expected that over long periods of time, these asset allocation
parameters will enable the plan to meet or exceed actuarial assumptions.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The investment guidelines prohibit certain types of
transactions, including the purchase of securities on margin, short-sale
transactions, the purchase of letter stock or other non-registered securities,
securities lending and any other investments or investment strategies
disallowed by ERISA or related regulations.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Equity securities of the plan did not include any
investment in the Company&#146;s common stock at December&nbsp;31, 2006 or January&nbsp;1,
2006.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In August&nbsp;2006, the Pension Protection Act of
2006 (the &#147;Act&#148;) was signed into law. The Act clarified funding rules&nbsp;and
rates for determining deficit reduction. As a result, the Company contributed
$2,150,000 to the Company&#146;s defined benefit cash balance pension plan during
the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2006. </font></p>
