 <p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:16.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 24.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">FRIENDLY ICE CREAM CORPORATION AND SUBSIDIARIES<br> NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS (Continued)</font></b></p>


<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">11.
PENSION PLAN (Continued)</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company does not
anticipate a contribution in 2007. Funding requirements for subsequent years
are uncertain and will significantly depend on whether the plan&#146;s actuary
changes any assumptions used to calculate plan funding levels, the actual
return on plan assets, changes in the employee groups covered by the plan, and
any legislative or regulatory changes affecting plan funding requirements. For
tax planning, financial planning, cash flow management or cost reduction
purposes the Company may increase, accelerate, decrease or delay contributions
to the plan to the extent permitted by law. Currently, the Company expects to
contribute approximately $3,500,000 in 2008.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The
following benefit payments, excluding any lump sum distributions, which reflect
expected future service, as appropriate, are expected to be paid (in
thousands):</font></p>

 <tr style="page-break-inside:avoid;">
  <td width="24" valign="bottom" style="border:none;border-bottom:solid windowtext 1.0pt;padding:0pt .7pt 0pt 0pt;width:17.8pt;">
  <p align="left" style="font-weight:bold;line-height:8.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt .0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:left;"><b><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:8.0pt;">Year</font></b></p>

<p style="line-height:1.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">12. POSTRETIREMENT MEDICAL
AND LIFE INSURANCE BENEFITS</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company provides medical and life insurance
benefits to certain groups of employees upon retirement. Eligible employees may
continue their coverage if they are receiving a pension benefit, are at least
55 years of age and have completed ten years of service. The plan requires
contributions for medical coverage from participants who retired after September&nbsp;1,
1989. Medical coverage may continue until age 65. Life insurance benefits are
contributory for participants who retired after July&nbsp;1, 2002. Medical
benefits under the plan are provided through the Company&#146;s general assets.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company uses a December&nbsp;31 measurement date
for the plan.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In October&nbsp;2006, the FASB issued SFAS No.&nbsp;158,
&#147;Employers&#146; Accounting for Defined Benefit Pension and Other Postretirement
Plans, an amendment of FASB Statements No.&nbsp;87, 88, 106 and 132(R)&#148; (&#147;SFAS No.&nbsp;158&#148;),
which requires an entity to: (a)&nbsp;recognize in its statement of financial
position an asset for a defined benefit postretirement plan&#146;s overfunded status
or a liability for a plan&#146;s underfunded status, (b)&nbsp;measure a defined
benefit postretirement plan&#146;s assets and obligations that determine its funded
status as of the end of the employer&#146;s fiscal year, and (c)&nbsp;recognize
changes in the funded status of a defined benefit postretirement plan in
comprehensive income in the year in which the changes occur. The requirement to
recognize the funded status of a defined benefit postretirement plan and the
disclosure requirements are effective for the Company&#146;s 2006 fiscal year.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The estimated net loss and prior service credit for
the postretirement medical and life insurance benefit plan that will be
amortized from accumulated other comprehensive income into net postretirement
medical and life insurance benefit cost during 2007 are $16,000 and $142,000,
respectively.</font></p>

<p style="line-height:1.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On December&nbsp;8, 2003, the Medicare Prescription
Drug, Improvement and Modernization Act of 2003 (the &#147;Act&#148;), which introduced a
Medicare prescription drug benefit, as well as a federal subsidy to sponsors of
retiree health care benefit plans that provide a benefit that is at least
actuarially equivalent to the Medicare benefit, was enacted. On May&nbsp;19,
2004, the FASB issued Financial Staff Position No.&nbsp;106-2, &#147;Accounting
and Disclosure Requirements Related to the Medicare Prescription Drug,
Improvement and Modernization Act of 2003&#148; (&#147;FSP 106-2&#148;) to discuss
certain accounting and disclosure issues raised by the Act. FSP 106-2
addresses accounting for the federal subsidy for the sponsors of single
employer postretirement health care plans and disclosure requirements for plans
for which the employer has not yet been able to determine actuarial
equivalency. Except for certain nonpublic entities, FSP 106-2 became
effective for the first interim or annual period beginning after June&nbsp;15,
2004 (the quarter ended September&nbsp;26, 2004 for the Company).</font></p>


 <p style="margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">F-43</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">
 <p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:16.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 24.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">FRIENDLY ICE CREAM CORPORATION AND SUBSIDIARIES<br> NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS (Continued)</font></b></p>


<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">12.
POSTRETIREMENT MEDICAL AND LIFE INSURANCE BENEFITS (Continued)</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Based on regulations
issued by the Centers for Medicare&nbsp;&amp; Medicaid Services, the Company
has concluded that, for certain participants, the benefits provided are at
least actuarially equivalent to benefits available through Medicare Part&nbsp;D.
The accumulated benefit obligation of the Company&#146;s postretirement medical and
life insurance plan at January&nbsp;1, 2006 decreased by $900,000 due to the
effect of the federal subsidy and the net periodic benefit cost for 2005 was
reduced by $99,900.</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">13. OTHER RETIREMENT
BENEFIT PLANS</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company&#146;s Employee
Savings and Investment Plan (the &#147;Plan&#148;) covers all eligible employees and is
intended to be qualified under Sections 401(a)&nbsp;and 401(k)&nbsp;of the
Internal Revenue Code. For the years ended December&nbsp;31, 2006, January&nbsp;1,
2006 and January&nbsp;2, 2005, the Company made matching contributions in an
amount equal to 75% of the sum of the participants&#146; contributions that do not
exceed 6% of the participant&#146;s compensation for employees above the position of
secondary management, as defined in the Plan. All employee contributions are
fully vested. Company contributions are vested at the completion of three years
of service or at retirement, death, disability or termination at age 65 or
over, as defined by the Plan. Company contributions and administrative expenses
for the Plan were $838,000, $866,000 and $972,000 for the years ended December&nbsp;31,
2006, January&nbsp;1, 2006 and January&nbsp;2, 2005, respectively.</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">14. INSURANCE RESERVES</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">At December&nbsp;31, 2006 and January&nbsp;1, 2006
insurance reserves of approximately $32,488,000 and $32,097,000, respectively,
had been recorded. Insurance reserves at December&nbsp;31, 2006 and January&nbsp;1,
2006 included RIC&#146;s reserves for the Company&#146;s insurance liabilities of
approximately $6,371,000 and $7,461,000, respectively. Reserves also included
accruals related to post employment benefits and postretirement medical and
life insurance benefits. While management believes these reserves were
adequate, it is reasonably possible that the ultimate liabilities may exceed
such estimates.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Classification
of the reserves was as follows (in thousands):</font></p>

 <p style="margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">F-44</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">
 <p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:16.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 24.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">FRIENDLY ICE CREAM CORPORATION AND SUBSIDIARIES<br> NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS (Continued)</font></b></p>


<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><font style="font-size:10.0pt;">14.
INSURANCE RESERVES</font> (Continued)</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The provision for
insurance reserves each year was actuarially determined and reflected amounts
for the current year as well as revisions in estimates to open reserves for
prior years. Payments included amounts paid on open claims for all years.</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">15. RELATED PARTY
TRANSACTIONS</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">While FICC&#146;s Chairman of the Board was an officer of
The Restaurant Company (&#147;TRC&#148;), FICC entered into a sublease for certain land,
building and equipment from a subsidiary of TRC. For the years ended December&nbsp;31,
2006, January&nbsp;1, 2006 and January&nbsp;2, 2005, rent expense related to
the sublease was approximately $71,000, $70,000 and $69,000, respectively.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company purchased certain food products used in
the normal course of business from a division of TRC at cost plus a mark-up.
For the years ended December&nbsp;31, 2006, January&nbsp;1, 2006 and January&nbsp;2,
2005, purchases were approximately $360,000, $353,000 and $340,000,
respectively.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On May&nbsp;22, 2006, The Ice Cream Company (&#147;TICC&#148;)
purchased, at fair market value, certain assets and leasehold rights for three
existing Company-operated restaurants located in Lancaster and York,
Pennsylvania. At closing, TICC was also granted an exclusive right to develop
six new Friendly&#146;s restaurants in Lancaster, Chester and Montgomery counties,
Pennsylvania by April&nbsp;2012. Gross proceeds from this transaction were
$1,725,000, of which $90,000 was for initial franchise fees, $90,000 was for
development fees and $1,545,000 was for the sale of certain assets and leasehold
rights at the three existing restaurants. During the year ended December&nbsp;31,
2006, the Company recorded $90,000 as franchise fee revenue and recognized a
gain of $1,146,000 related to the sale of the assets.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The owners of TICC are family members of the Company&#146;s
Chairman of the Board of Directors. Prior to the closing of this transaction on
May&nbsp;22, 2006, TICC operated three Friendly&#146;s restaurants under franchise
agreements with Friendly&#146;s Restaurants Franchise,&nbsp;Inc. (&#147;FRFI&#148;), a
subsidiary of Friendly&#146;s. The terms of the franchise agreements with TICC are
identical in all material respects to the terms generally offered to unrelated
franchisees of FRFI in the ordinary course of Friendly&#146;s business.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">TICC purchases from Friendly&#146;s certain food products used
in the normal course of its franchise business. During 2006, 2005 and 2004,
TICC paid Friendly&#146;s $3,405,000, $2,110,000 and $2,080,000, respectively, for
franchise royalty fees, marketing fees, food purchases and miscellaneous other
products and services.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During August&nbsp;2003, Friendly&#146;s entered into a
single restaurant franchise agreement with Treats of Huntersville LLC (&#147;Treats&#148;).
The owner of Treats is a family member of the Company&#146;s Chairman of the Board
of Directors. The transaction was a standard agreement in compliance with the
terms and conditions of the Uniform Franchise Offering Circular allowing Treats
to operate one location. The location, which was initially opened by a former
franchisee but closed in July&nbsp;2002, was reopened by Treats in August&nbsp;2003.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Treats purchases from
Friendly&#146;s certain food products used in the normal course of its franchise
business. During 2006, 2005 and 2004, Treats paid Friendly&#146;s $439,000, $428,000
and $422,000, respectively, for franchise royalty fees, marketing fees, food
purchases and miscellaneous other products and services.</font></p>


 <p style="margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">F-45</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">

<!-- SEQ.=1,FOLIO='F-45',FILE='C:\fc\6164713283_D11086_1801640\5770-1-fy.htm',USER='jmsproofassembler',CD='Mar  2 06:48 2007' -->
<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">
 <p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:16.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 24.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">FRIENDLY ICE CREAM CORPORATION AND SUBSIDIARIES<br> NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS (Continued)</font></b></p>


<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">16. COMMITMENTS AND
CONTINGENCIES</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company is a party to various legal proceedings
arising in the ordinary course of business which management believes, after
consultation with legal counsel, will not have a material adverse effect on the
Company&#146;s consolidated financial position or future operating results.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On February&nbsp;25, 2003, S. Prestley Blake (&#147;Blake&#148;),
holder of approximately 12% of the Company&#146;s outstanding common stock, sued
Friendly&#146;s and its Chairman in a purported derivative action in Hampden
Superior Court, Massachusetts. The suit alleges breach of fiduciary duty and
misappropriation of corporate assets in that Friendly&#146;s paid certain expenses
relating to a corporate jet and the Chairman&#146;s use of that jet and use of an
office in Illinois. The suit seeks to require the Chairman to reimburse
Friendly&#146;s and for Friendly&#146;s to pay Blake&#146;s attorneys&#146; fees. Friendly&#146;s and
its Chairman have denied Blake&#146;s allegations and are vigorously defending the
lawsuit.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On June&nbsp;27, 2005, Mr.&nbsp;Blake sent a demand
letter to the Company&#146;s Board of Directors demanding that its Board of
Directors address his concerns and beliefs that are subject to the litigation
filed on February&nbsp;25, 2003. </font>On July&nbsp;14, 2005, the Company&#146;s Board of Directors formed a
special litigation committee consisting solely of independent directors (the &#147;Committee&#148;)
to investigate the concerns and beliefs raised in Blake&#146;s demand letter dated June&nbsp;27,
2005. The Committee issued its report on October&nbsp;24, 2005 and a
supplemental report on November&nbsp;30, 2005. Based on its findings, the
Committee filed a motion to dismiss the claims made by Mr.&nbsp;Blake. On
May&nbsp;24, 2006, the Court denied the Committee&#146;s motion to dismiss and
allowed the joinder, as defendants, of current Board members Steven L. Ezzes,
Michael J. Daly and Burton J. Manning, and former Board member Charles A.
Ledsinger,&nbsp;Jr., and The Restaurant Company, The Restaurant Holding
Corporation and TRC Realty, LLC.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On July&nbsp;26, 2006, director defendants Michael J.
Daly, Steven L. Ezzes, and Burton J. Manning, and former director defendant
Charles A. Ledsinger,&nbsp;Jr., filed motions to dismiss the claims brought
against them for failure to state a claim on the grounds that both the
exculpatory provision in the Company&#146;s Restated Articles of Organization and
the business judgment rule&nbsp;barred the plaintiff&#146;s claims. On December&nbsp;20,
2006, the Court granted the directors&#146; motion and dismissed from the Blake
litigation director defendants Michael J. Daly, Steven L. Ezzes, Burton J.
Manning and former director defendant Charles A. Ledsinger,&nbsp;Jr. The Court
has set a deadline for fact discovery of May&nbsp;31, 2007, with a trial, if
necessary, to begin on January&nbsp;7, 2008. </font>Friendly&#146;s and its Chairman have denied
Blake&#146;s allegations and are vigorously defending the lawsuit.</p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As of December&nbsp;31, 2006, the Company had
commitments to purchase approximately $111,390,000 of raw materials, food
products and supplies used in the normal course of business. The majority of
the commitments cover periods of one to 12 months. Most of these commitments
are noncancelable.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On February&nbsp;7, 2007,
the Company entered into a 10 year contract to purchase approximately $340,000
in liquid nitrogen annually.</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">17. SEGMENT REPORTING</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Operating segments are components of an enterprise
about which separate financial information is available that is evaluated
regularly by the chief operating decision-maker, or decision-making group, in
deciding how to allocate resources and in assessing performance. The Company&#146;s
operating segments include restaurant, foodservice and franchise. The revenues
from these segments include both sales to unaffiliated customers and
intersegment sales, which generally are accounted for on a basis consistent
with </font></p>


 <p style="margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">F-46</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">

<!-- SEQ.=1,FOLIO='F-46',FILE='C:\fc\6164713283_D11086_1801640\5770-1-fy.htm',USER='jmsproofassembler',CD='Mar  2 06:48 2007' -->
<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">
 <p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:16.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 24.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">FRIENDLY ICE CREAM CORPORATION AND SUBSIDIARIES<br> NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS (Continued)</font></b></p>


<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><font style="font-size:10.0pt;">17. SEGMENT
REPORTING</font> (Continued)</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">sales to unaffiliated
customers. Intersegment sales and other intersegment transactions have been
eliminated in the accompanying consolidated financial statements.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company&#146;s restaurants target families with
children and adults who desire a reasonably-priced meal in a full-service
setting. The Company&#146;s menu offers a broad selection of freshly-prepared
foods which appeal to customers throughout all dayparts. The menu currently
features over 100 items comprised of a broad selection of breakfast, lunch,
dinner and afternoon and evening snack items. Foodservice operations
manufactures premium ice cream dessert products and distributes such
manufactured products and purchased finished goods to Company-operated and
franchised restaurants. Additionally, it sells premium ice cream dessert
products to distributors and retail locations. The Company&#146;s franchise segment
includes a royalty based on franchise restaurant revenue. In addition, the
Company receives rental income from various franchised restaurants. The Company
does not allocate general and administrative expenses associated with its
headquarters operations to any business segment. These costs include expenses
of the following functions: legal, accounting, personnel not directly related
to a segment, information systems and other headquarter activities.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The accounting policies of the operating segments are
the same as those described in the summary of significant accounting policies
except that the financial results for the foodservice operating segment, prior
to intersegment eliminations, have been prepared using a management approach,
which is consistent with the basis and manner in which the Company&#146;s management
internally reviews financial information. Using this approach, the Company
evaluates performance based on stand-alone operating segment income (loss)
before income taxes and generally accounts for intersegment sales and transfers
as if the sales or transfers were to third parties, that is, at current market
prices.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Adjusted EBITDA represents net income (loss) from
continuing operations before (i)&nbsp;(provision for) benefit from income
taxes, (ii)&nbsp;interest expense, net, (iii)&nbsp;depreciation and
amortization, (iv)&nbsp;write-downs of property and equipment, (v)&nbsp;net
periodic pension cost and (vi)&nbsp;other non-cash items. Adjusted EBITDA
is a non-GAAP financial measure. The Company has included information
concerning adjusted EBITDA in this Form&nbsp;10-K because the Company&#146;s
management incentive plan pays bonuses based on achieving operating segment
adjusted EBITDA targets and the Company believes that such information is used
by certain investors as one measure of a company&#146;s historical ability to
service debt. Adjusted EBITDA should not be considered as an alternative to, or
more meaningful than, earnings (loss) from continuing operations or other
traditional indications of the Company&#146;s operating performance.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During the year ended December&nbsp;31,
2006, the Company stopped the allocation of one financial department to the
restaurant segment as it was determined that this department should be reported
with general and administrative corporate expenses. Adjusted EBITDA and income
(loss) from continuing operations before (provision for) benefit from income
taxes have been restated to remove the costs associated with this department of
$0.2 million for both years ended January&nbsp;1, 2006 and January&nbsp;2,
2005.</font></p>

<p style="line-height:1.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">18. INSURANCE RECOVERY</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On January&nbsp;27, 2006, the Company initiated
litigation against its insurance carrier to recoup defense expenses related to
the Blake litigation. On September&nbsp;27, 2006, the Company entered into a settlement
agreement with its insurance carrier which provides, in part, for 1) a lump sum
payment to settle past disputed expenses and 2) clarification of coverage of
future defense expenses related to this matter.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During the year ended December&nbsp;31,
2006, the Company received insurance recoveries of $1,596,000, of which
$1,428,000 was pursuant to the settlement agreement with the Company&#146;s
insurance carrier, related to costs and expenses incurred related to the above
matter. Additionally, the Company has recorded a receivable for insurance
recoveries to the extent defense expenses have been incurred and realization of
a related insurance claim is probable. As of December&nbsp;31, 2006, the
receivable for insurance recoveries totaled $170,000.</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">19. GAIN ON LITIGATION
SETTLEMENT</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In January&nbsp;2004, the
Company reached a settlement in a lawsuit filed against a former administrator
of one of the Company&#146;s benefit plans. The settlement was based on the
administrator&#146;s alleged failure to adhere to the terms of a contract and
resulted in a one-time payment to the Company of $3,775,000, which was received
on April&nbsp;2, 2004. As a result of this lawsuit, the Company incurred
professional fees of approximately $500,000 which were included in the
consolidated statement of operations for the year ended December&nbsp;28, 2003
and an additional $131,000 in professional fees that were offset against the
payment in the accompanying consolidated statement of operations for the year
ended January&nbsp;2, 2005.</font></p>

 <p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:16.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 24.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">FRIENDLY ICE CREAM CORPORATION AND SUBSIDIARIES<br> NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS (Continued)</font></b></p>


<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><font style="font-size:10.0pt;">20.
QUARTERLY FINANCIAL DATA (UNAUDITED)</font> (Continued)</font></b></p>

<div style="margin:0pt 0pt .0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><hr size="1" width="160" noshade color="black" align="left" style="width:120.0pt;"></div>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 20.0pt;text-indent:-20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(a)</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>During the fourth
quarter of 2005, the Company entered a three-year cumulative loss position and
revised its projections of the amount and timing of profitability in future
periods. As a result, the Company increased its valuation allowance by
approximately $26,729,000 ($22,184,000 to income tax expense and $4,545,000 to
stockholders&#146; deficit) to reduce the carrying value of deferred tax assets to
zero (Note 8).</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt 20.0pt;text-indent:-20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(b)</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>The
fourth quarters in 2006 and 2005 included asset impairment write-downs of $198,000
and $2,190,000, respectively (Note 5).</p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">21. SUPPLEMENTAL CONSOLIDATING
FINANCIAL INFORMATION</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">FICC&#146;s obligation related to the Senior Notes is
guaranteed fully and unconditionally by one of FICC&#146;s wholly owned
subsidiaries. There are no restrictions on FICC&#146;s ability to obtain dividends
or other distributions of funds from this subsidiary, except those imposed by
applicable law. The following supplemental financial information sets forth, on
a consolidating basis, balance sheets, statements of operations and statements
of cash flows for FICC (the &#147;Parent Company&#148;), Friendly&#146;s Restaurants Franchise,&nbsp;Inc.
(the &#147;Guarantor Subsidiary&#148;) and Friendly&#146;s International,&nbsp;Inc.,
Restaurant Insurance Corporation, Friendly&#146;s Realty I, LLC, Friendly&#146;s Realty
II, LLC and Friendly&#146;s Realty III, LLC (collectively, the &#147;Non-guarantor
Subsidiaries&#148;). All of the limited liability companies&#146; (the &#147;LLCs&#148;) assets
were owned by the LLCs, which are separate entities with separate creditors
which will be entitled to be satisfied out of the LLCs&#146; assets. Separate
complete financial statements and other disclosures of the Guarantor Subsidiary
as of December&nbsp;31, 2006 and January&nbsp;1, 2006 and for the years ended December&nbsp;31,
2006 and January&nbsp;1, 2006 and January&nbsp;2, 2005 were not presented
because management has determined that such information is not material to
investors.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Investments in subsidiaries are accounted for by the
Parent Company on the equity method for purposes of the supplemental
consolidating presentation. Earnings of the subsidiaries are, therefore,
reflected in the Parent Company&#146;s investment accounts and earnings. The
principal elimination entries eliminate the Parent Company&#146;s investments in
subsidiaries and intercompany balances and transactions.</font></p>
